clue.text: Discharge exploding so deep

indicators.note: something exploding is blown apart, so the letters of the two words are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A report about something going off with a deep boom, perhaps a depth charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a noun for an explosion, but it is a verb: to dismiss someone from office.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a ruler or official is to remove them from their post, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Check wall on compound

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another means it comes first, above it

parts.note: a dam is a wall holding back water
a pen is an enclosure or compound for animals

explanation.surface: An instruction to inspect the wall around a prison or military compound.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something, such as enthusiasm, is to restrain or deaden it, a synonym.

clue.text: Crazed mob suspend on and off

parts.note: a posse is a band or mob of people

indicators.note: taking letters on and off means every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A frenzied crowd intermittently halting proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone possessed behaves as if gripped by a demon, wild and frenzied: a synonym.

clue.text: Ship's crew in endless ocean run

indicators.note: the crew word goes in the middle of the shortened ocean word
endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the sea is the ocean
a team is a crew working together
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A ship's crew sailing across a seemingly limitless ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'Ship's' stands for 'is' and links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a vessel powered by steam, so a kind of ship.

clue.text: Grand Canyon, American, split by Colorado's right bank

indicators.note: the pair of pieces is broken apart by a letter placed between them

parts.note: a gorge is a deep narrow valley, a canyon

indicators.note: the right-hand edge of the word, its final letter

explanation.surface: The Grand Canyon in America, cut through by the Colorado River.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand Canyon' reads as a place name, but 'Grand' is the definition and 'Canyon' starts the wordplay; the right bank of Colorado is its last letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and gorgeous both describe something magnificent or splendid in appearance.

clue.text: Has planted first of seeds to appear last

indicators.text: first of seeds to appear last
indicators.note: the opening letter of seeds is moved from the front to the end

parts.note: seeds that are sown have been planted

explanation.surface: A gardener has planted seeds and waits for them to come up.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have it as a possession, so a synonym.

clue.text: State of danger possibly covering area

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation, covering it
possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A country in a state of danger, perhaps one threatening a whole area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges DANGER as GRENDA, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island nation, so an example of a state.

clue.text: Work on twitch of the eye

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: Treating a nervous twitch of the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective meaning relating to the eye or to vision.

clue.text: Walk on edges of narrowest grating

indicators.note: in a down clue the walking word sits on top of the letters that follow

parts.note: to stride is to walk with long steps

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Stepping carefully along the edge of a narrow metal grating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like a metal grille, but it is the adjective for a harsh sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident noise is harsh and grating to the ear, a synonym.

clue.text: That man is after the old lady's pounds

indicators.note: the first-written piece comes after the second in the answer

parts.note: ma is mother, the old lady, so ma's
contracted, he is becomes he's

explanation.surface: A man spending his mother's money in pounds sterling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' suggests money, but it is a verb: beats or crushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pounds and mashes both mean crushes into a pulp, as with potatoes.

clue.text: Perchance story will include old relative

indicators.note: the two words together will include the letters needed, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A tale told about a long-gone family member, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear, a family member from generations ago.

clue.text: Stone fire support keeping cool back

indicators.note: the grate word holds the reversed piece inside it

parts.note: a grate holds up the fire in a fireplace

indicators.note: back means the cool word is written backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A stone fireplace with a support that keeps the cold at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone fire' reads like a stone hearth, but 'fire support' belongs together as the thing in a fireplace that holds the coals.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock, an example of stone.

clue.text: European capital housing churchman's backed eternally

indicators.note: backed means the whole assembly is written in reverse
the capital holds the churchman inside it

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
Rev is the title of a clergyman, the Reverend

explanation.surface: A European capital that has long been home to clergymen, Rome perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns round the whole assembly, not just the churchman, so the solver must build the string first and then read it in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore means for all time, forever, a synonym of eternally.

clue.text: Issued digital record, keeping single off

parts.note: ran, as in issued or flowed out

indicators.note: the record letters hold the single letter between them

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a digital recording
I is the Roman numeral one, single

explanation.surface: A music label releases an album but holds back the single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of the surface but is the definition: food gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is off has spoiled, and rancid describes spoiled, foul-smelling fat or butter.

clue.text: Group still to engage name tenor

indicators.note: to engage is to take in and hold, so the still word holds the two letters

parts.note: quiet means still or calm

explanation.surface: A music group is still to hire a tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: A quintet is a group of five, especially of musicians.

clue.text: Choking from lungs' atria not working

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A medical report: choking caused by the lungs and heart chambers failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' reads as one phrase about failing organs, but 'not' is part of the fodder and 'working' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangulation is the act of choking by squeezing the throat.

clue.text: In driving rain edifice is immovable

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A building stands firm in driving rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrained describes something so deeply fixed it cannot be shifted.

clue.text: Tabloid declines to carry right cheap articles

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: the declines word carries the letter inside it

parts.note: dies, as in dies away or fades

explanation.surface: A tabloid refuses to run adverts for bargain goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundries are miscellaneous small items of little value, odds and ends.

clue.text: Inanely grinned at nudes losing sweetheart's sympathy

indicators.note: doing something inanely is doing it foolishly, so the letters are jumbled
losing means a letter is dropped from the jumbled pool

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Someone grinning foolishly at naked people loses their partner's sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inanely' rearranges GRINNED AT NUDES, and 'losing' takes out the E at the heart of sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Understanding is sympathetic awareness of how someone else feels.

clue.text: Queen in charge with powerful King, say

parts.note: R is short for regina, Latin for queen
hard as in strong or powerful, a hard punch

explanation.surface: A queen running things alongside a mighty king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the definition as an example: there have been several kings of England called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard is the name of several English kings, so a king by way of example.

clue.text: Current performance, embracing former wife, is not true

indicators.note: the two pieces together wrap around the former wife

parts.note: in means current or fashionable
an act is a performance
an ex is a former wife

explanation.surface: Rumours that a current show features someone's ex-wife are false.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is imprecise, so not strictly true or accurate.

clue.text: Almost new in the morning

parts.note: early means in the morning

explanation.surface: Something nearly brand new first thing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly and almost are direct synonyms meaning not quite.

clue.text: Frank Capra did this

definitions.meaning: Frank Capra was a film director, so this is what he did to films

explanation.surface: Film director Frank Capra and something he did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank Capra' reads as one name, but 'Frank' is a definition on its own; Capra directed It's a Wonderful Life.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank is being straightforward, and directing films was Capra's job.

clue.text: River's height regarding eastern river

parts.note: R is short for river
on means about or regarding

explanation.surface: A note on a river's height with regard to an eastern river.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'River' gives only its letter R; the definition is the final 'river'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major waterway flowing through Switzerland and France.

clue.text: Charge headed over English wicket

indicators.note: over means the word is turned over, written backwards

parts.note: led, as in headed or was in front
a wicket is a small gate

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batsman charged and headed the ball onto his wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' and 'wicket' suggest cricket, but a wicket here is a small gate or door.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to charge someone else with doing it.

clue.text: Performing animal seen in impressive ring?

definitions.meaning: a circus or zoo creature that balances balls and claps its flippers
a signet ring carries an engraved design pressed into wax, so it makes impressions

explanation.surface: A trained animal seen in an amazing circus ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressive' is a pun: such a ring makes impressions in wax.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a sea mammal trained in circuses; the ring kind is a signet bearing an emblem.

clue.text: Single ladies to split up

indicators.note: split up means the letters are broken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: Single women deciding to break up with their partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means alone or set apart, so single in that sense.

clue.text: Character of country house reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: a manor is a large country house with its lands

explanation.surface: The character of a rural house, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner can mean kind or sort, its character, as in what manner of thing.

clue.text: It delays travelling round the clock

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Travelling causes delays all day and night.
explanation.definitionFit: Working round the clock means continuously, without stopping, which is what steadily conveys.

clue.text: Somewhat tedious or dull generating yawns initially

definitions.text: Somewhat tedious or dull generating yawns initially

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Something rather boring that sets people yawning.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as spelling it out from its first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodgy describes heavy, dull, uninspired writing or company that bores people.
